## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Adoption should preserve files when the incoming values already match: it currently records a change and rewrites an unchanged configuration. This review traced merge behavior and file writes, and read all existing and added tests without running them.

## Changes
The pull request adds an `adopt` option that updates existing settings and records their keys, plus tests for adoption and replacement.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — Skip adoption writes when the value is unchanged — With `{"theme":"dark"}` already stored, `merge(path, {"theme": "dark"}, adopt=True)` reports `["theme"]` and reformats the file despite no setting changing. The adoption branch appends the key unconditionally, triggering the write at line 23; replacement checks equality first. This contradicts the module’s stated preservation of untouched configuration files. — Callers receive a false change signal, and adopting an already matching setting unnecessarily changes the file’s bytes.
